prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

NEW DELHI, India (CNN) -- Indian police swiftly handled a "security scare" at New Delhi's major airport early Friday amid heightened concern in the wake of last week's terror attack in which gunmen killed 179 people in Mumbai. An Indian soldier joins the beefed up security detail at New Delhi airport. New Delhi police spokesman Rajan Bhagat said police responded to reports of gunfire at Indira Gandhi International Airport but found no casualties or damage. Bhagat said there was "no terror threat." "And there's no cause of panic," he added. Uday Banerjee, the head of India's Central Industrial Security Force, told reporters at the airport that something sounding like gunshots was heard, but no one saw anything and no bullet casings were found. Indian authorities stepped up security at the nation's airports on Thursday after receiving intelligence reports that terrorists might be planning an air attack. At Indira Gandhi, four armed police stood guard at each entrance, and people waiting for arriving passengers were not allowed inside.  Watch what triggered the security scare there » . "There have been intelligence inputs about some terrorist activity, and therefore security has been tightened (at airports)," civil aviation spokesperson Moushmi Chakraborty told CNN.  Watch heightened anxiety after the attacks » . Police beefed up security at all airports including in the capital New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Bangalore, Chakraborty said. A spokesman for the Indian Navy, Cmdr. Nirad Sinha, also confirmed to CNN that security officials had received warnings about an airborne attack.  Watch more on increase in security » . The Press Trust of India, a nonprofit newspaper cooperative, said that reports had suggested that terrorists could have sneaked into the country to carry out strikes on the anniversary of the Babri mosque demolition. The mosque -- one of the largest in the Uttar Pradesh state -- was destroyed on December 6, 1992, by Hindu nationalists who believe it was built on the site of an existing temple. On Wednesday India's defense minister met with the chiefs of the army, air force and navy and discussed what the ministry in a news statement called "possible terror threats from air." The officials also discussed the country's coastal security plans and how to tighten security along the military line of control dividing the disputed region of Kashmir between India and Pakistan to "prevent infiltration of terrorists," the statement said. India ranks among the countries where terrorism is most common, according to the U.S. State Department. CNN's Harmeet Shah Singh and Sara Sidner contributed to this report.

NEW DELHI, India (CNN) — Police in India moved quickly early Friday to deal with what officials described as a “security scare” at New Delhi’s main airport, as the country remained on high alert after the previous week’s terrorist assault in Mumbai, where gunmen killed 179 people.

An Indian soldier was part of the expanded security presence at New Delhi’s airport.

Rajan Bhagat, a spokesman for New Delhi police, said officers went to Indira Gandhi International Airport after receiving reports of shots being fired. However, they found no injuries and no damage. Bhagat said there was “no terror threat,” adding, “And there’s no cause of panic.”

Uday Banerjee, who heads India’s Central Industrial Security Force, told journalists at the airport that a noise resembling gunfire had been heard. But he said nobody saw anything, and investigators found no spent bullet shells.

Authorities in India increased security at airports across the country on Thursday after intelligence warnings indicated that terrorists might be preparing an attack involving aircraft.

At Indira Gandhi International Airport, four armed officers were stationed at every entrance, and people waiting to meet arriving travelers were kept from entering the terminal.

Civil aviation spokeswoman Moushmi Chakraborty told CNN that security had been strengthened at airports because of intelligence “inputs” pointing to possible terrorist activity.

Chakraborty said police had reinforced security at all airports, including those in New Delhi, Mumbai, Chennai and Bangalore.

Cmdr. Nirad Sinha, a spokesman for the Indian Navy, also told CNN that security authorities had received alerts about a possible attack from the air.

The Press Trust of India, a nonprofit newspaper cooperative, reported that earlier accounts suggested terrorists may have entered the country secretly to stage attacks around the anniversary of the destruction of the Babri mosque.

The mosque, one of the biggest in Uttar Pradesh state, was demolished on December 6, 1992, by Hindu nationalists who believed it had been constructed on the location of a pre-existing temple.

On Wednesday, India’s defense minister held talks with the heads of the army, air force and navy. According to a statement from the ministry, they discussed “possible terror threats from air.”

The statement said the officials also reviewed India’s coastal security arrangements and considered ways to strengthen security along the military line of control that separates the disputed Kashmir region between India and Pakistan, in order to “prevent infiltration of terrorists.”

According to the U.S. State Department, India is among the countries most frequently affected by terrorism.

CNN’s Harmeet Shah Singh and Sara Sidner contributed to this report.

**Security scare at New Delhi airport after reports of gunfire**

**NEW DELHI, India** — Indian police responded to a security scare at Indira Gandhi International Airport early Friday after reports of gunfire near the facility, officials said, prompting a swift deployment amid heightened alert following the Mumbai terror attacks.

Police and airport security personnel rushed to the scene after witnesses reported hearing shots near the airport area. Authorities cordoned off parts of the airport and searched the vicinity, but there were no immediate reports of casualties or confirmed evidence of an attack.

Flights continued to operate, though security checks were intensified and passengers faced delays as officers conducted additional screening.

The incident came as India remained on edge after the deadly attacks in Mumbai, where gunmen targeted luxury hotels, a Jewish center, a train station and other locations, killing more than 160 people. Since then, security has been increased at airports, railway stations, government buildings and other sensitive sites across the country.

New Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport is one of India’s busiest and a key hub for domestic and international travel. Authorities said they were treating the reports seriously but urged the public not to panic while the investigation continued.

“We are verifying the reports and have increased security as a precaution,” a police official said.

No group claimed responsibility, and officials did not immediately confirm whether gunshots had actually been fired.

**Gunfire Reports at New Delhi Airport Prompt Security Response Amid Heightened Terror Alert**

**New Delhi** — Reports of gunfire near New Delhi’s Indira Gandhi International Airport triggered a swift response from police and security agencies, adding to an already tense security climate in the Indian capital as authorities remained on alert around the anniversary of the Babri mosque demolition.

According to initial reports, security personnel were alerted after sounds resembling gunshots were heard in or near the airport area. Police and airport security forces moved quickly to assess the situation, secure sensitive zones and verify whether any firing had occurred. Officials said checks were carried out across the affected area, including airport access points and nearby roads.

Delhi Police officials stated that no immediate evidence of an active attack had been confirmed. Security forces, including airport protection units, were deployed as a precaution while investigators reviewed witness accounts and surveillance footage.

“There is no confirmed terror incident at the airport at this stage,” a police official said, according to local reporting. “Security personnel responded immediately after receiving information, and the area was checked.”

Airport security agencies also said operations were being monitored closely. While there were no immediate reports of casualties, authorities maintained an enhanced security posture at the airport, one of India’s busiest and most sensitive transport hubs.

The incident came at a time of broader concern over possible terror threats linked to the anniversary of the demolition of the Babri mosque in Ayodhya on December 6, 1992. The mosque’s destruction by Hindu nationalist activists sparked widespread communal violence across India and remains one of the most sensitive flashpoints in the country’s modern political history.

Indian security agencies routinely increase vigilance around the anniversary, particularly in major cities, religious sites, transport hubs and government installations. Officials have warned in past years that militant groups could attempt attacks or exploit communal tensions during the period.

In New Delhi, police have typically intensified patrols, checked vehicles at key intersections and deployed additional personnel around crowded markets, transit stations and areas considered vulnerable to unrest or sabotage. Security has also been tightened around airports, railway stations and diplomatic areas.

A senior security official said agencies were treating all suspicious reports seriously, given the threat environment. “Any information related to firing, suspicious movement or unattended objects is being verified immediately,” the official said. “There is heightened alertness because of the date and the possibility of attempts to create panic.”

The Babri mosque anniversary has long been associated with heightened political and religious sensitivities. The demolition led to riots that killed thousands and reshaped Indian politics, contributing to the rise of Hindu nationalist movements and deepening communal divisions. Although the site is now being redeveloped following a Supreme Court ruling that cleared the way for a Hindu temple, the anniversary continues to draw attention from both law enforcement and political groups.

Authorities urged the public not to spread unverified information, particularly on social media, where rumors of attacks or firing can quickly create panic. Police said official updates would be issued as necessary.

Airport operations were reported to be under close watch, though officials did not immediately announce major disruptions. Passengers were advised to cooperate with security checks and allow extra time for travel if moving through the airport area.

The investigation into the reported gunfire remained ongoing, with police working to determine whether the sounds were caused by actual firing, a security drill, a mechanical noise or another source. Officials emphasized that there was no confirmed indication of a coordinated attack but said security would remain elevated as a precaution.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.output:
**Heightened terrorism fears prompt increased airport security across India**

**By [Reporter Name], CNN**  
**New Delhi, India**

India has tightened security at airports and other key transportation hubs amid heightened fears of possible terrorist attacks, including warnings that militants could attempt an air attack, officials said.

Security has been increased at major airports across the country, with additional screening of passengers, tighter checks on baggage and vehicles, and a more visible deployment of armed security personnel. Authorities have also stepped up surveillance around airport perimeters and other sensitive locations, according to Indian security officials.

The measures follow intelligence warnings suggesting that terrorist groups may be planning attacks aimed at aviation targets or other high-profile sites. Officials have not publicly detailed the nature of the threat, but said security agencies are treating the alerts seriously.

In New Delhi, senior government and defense officials held meetings to review the security situation and assess preparedness. The discussions included officials from India’s home ministry, defense establishment and intelligence agencies, according to government sources.

India has remained on alert following previous terrorist attacks on transportation networks, hotels, government buildings and crowded public spaces. Aviation security is a particular concern because of the potential for mass casualties and international impact.

Passengers at several airports reported longer lines and more intensive checks, though flights were continuing to operate. Airport officials urged travelers to arrive early and cooperate with security personnel.

The government has not announced any specific shutdowns or flight cancellations tied to the threat alerts, but officials said security measures could be adjusted depending on intelligence assessments.

Indian authorities routinely increase security ahead of major holidays, political events or after intelligence warnings. However, the latest measures come amid broader regional concerns about militant activity and the possibility of attacks intended to draw global attention.

Officials said there was no reason for panic but emphasized that vigilance remained essential.

CNN correspondents **Harmeet Shah Singh** and **Sara Sidner** contributed to this report.
